limit_order_match_in_progress.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder

matched_base_amount.meaning: matched base amount of the limit order match
matched_base_amount.checkpoint: before zero-cost validation during limit order matching

matched_quote_amount.meaning: matched quote amount of the limit order match
matched_quote_amount.checkpoint: before zero-cost validation during limit order matching

matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: matched base amount and matched quote amount have no overlapping 1-bits (e.g., base = 256 and quote in 1..255, or 40 & 21)
matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.checkpoint: before zero-cost validation during limit order matching

matched_base_nonzero.checkpoint: before zero-cost validation during limit order matching

matched_quote_nonzero.checkpoint: before zero-cost validation during limit order matching

rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.meaning: the legitimate limit order match is rejected as a zero-cost trade

all_limit_order_matching_affected.meaning: the effect applies to ALL limit order matching, both partial and full matches, while fill orders remain unaffected

assumptions: Matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities of the limit order match at the validation checkpoint.
The zero-cost rejection is a distinct observable outcome of the matching validation.

unresolved.description: The report states the disjoint-1-bits condition only qualitatively with examples (base = 256 and quote in 1..255, or 40 & 21); the exact bitwise expression and its operands are not quoted, so it is encoded as a grounded Boolean rather than a bitwise formula.
The exact zero-cost check expression and its operands are not fully quoted in prose; the rejection outcome is encoded as a grounded Boolean.

limitations: Caller identity and authorization for triggering limit order matching are not stated; the condition omits them.
Whether matched amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state is not specified.
The impact text describes scope (all limit order matching, partial and full) rather than a concrete revert event; the V witness encodes the zero-cost rejection plus the scope qualifier.
